chunks: From him, from Ja'far, he raised it to Mu'alla ibn Khunays: that he said,

To Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), I said: 'I intended to sell gold bullion in Medina, but it was not bought from me except for dinars. Is it permissible for me to make copper the difference between them?' He said, 'If you must do it, let the copper be by weight.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling gold bullion for gold coins with a difference of copper?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the application of the riba al-fadl rule for gold, where Imam al-Sadiq permits an unequal exchange if the surplus is compensated by copper, provided the copper is measured by weight rather than volume or count. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on precise measurement (wazn) to prevent hidden usury in commodity trades, distinguishing it from the stricter 'hand-to-hand' (qabd) requirement often cited in other schools for same-genus exchanges.
